index.operations/s3/get-metadata-split-encoded: S3 returns a long value as several RFC 2047 encoded words, separated by spaces. Decode each and join them without the spaces.
index.operations/s3/get-missing: get missing. A client reports it as not_found: the object is absent
index.operations/s3/get-range-empty: Read a range of no bytes, whose start equals its end. HTTP has no form for it: bytes=5-4 is inverted, and the service ignores it and sends the whole object. A client may refuse it instead
index.operations/s3/get-range-of-empty-object: Report a range read of an empty object as 416 InvalidRange: no range of it can be satisfied, not even its first byte
index.operations/s3/get-range-past-the-end: Read a range that ends past the object, which the service clips to the object's end. Report the window it served from Content-Range, bytes 28-29/30, so that the caller sees the range was clipped
index.operations/s3/get-slow-down: Report a 503 SlowDown answer as an error, after at most 5 retries
index.operations/s3/get-tagging: Read the tags of an object
index.operations/s3/get-tagging-none: Report no tags for an object without any, which S3 answers with an empty TagSet
index.operations/s3/get-temporary-redirect: Report a 307 TemporaryRedirect as an error
index.operations/s3/get-unauthenticated: Report the service authorization error for this operation; signature acceptance is tested separately.
index.operations/s3/get-wrong-region: Report a 301 PermanentRedirect from an endpoint in another region as an error
index.operations/s3/head-bucket-missing: Report a HEAD of an object in a missing bucket as missing, not not_found. S3 answers 404 without a body, the same answer as for a missing object, so a client cannot tell that the object is absent
index.operations/s3/head-content-properties: Return the stored content properties from a HEAD
index.operations/s3/head-if-unmodified-since-p: Refuse a HEAD with 412 when the object changed after If-Unmodified-Since
index.operations/s3/head-missing: Report a HEAD answered 404 as not_found or missing. Its answer has no body, so it cannot say whether the object or the bucket is absent
index.operations/s3/head-storage-class: Read the storage class of an object
index.operations/s3/list-all-empty: Report an empty bucket as an empty listing
index.operations/s3/list-all-pages: Follow each page's continuation token until a page is not truncated
index.operations/s3/list-bad-marker: Report S3's 400 InvalidArgument for a continuation token it did not issue
index.operations/s3/list-bucket-missing: Report 404 NoSuchBucket for a bucket that does not exist. A client reports it as container_not_found: the bucket or container is absent, not the object
index.operations/s3/list-checksum-algorithm: Report each listed object's checksum algorithm as one name; S3 keeps one checksum per object, the one a write sent or else CRC64NVME, and lists one ChecksumAlgorithm
index.operations/s3/list-delimited: Send the delimiter, and report the keys it groups as common prefixes, not as entries
index.operations/s3/list-empty: Report a prefix with no objects as no entries, no prefixes and an empty continuation token
index.operations/s3/list-encoded-names: Ask for encoding-type=url, and decode each name once: + is a space and %2B a plus. Without it S3 writes U+0001 as , which XML 1.0 forbids, and a CR that XML turns into LF
index.operations/s3/list-encoding-ignored: Read the keys as sent when a service ignores encoding-type=url and the page has no EncodingType; a % that begins no escape is text, as in URL percent-decoding
index.operations/s3/list-entry-properties: Report each listed object's last-modified time as RFC 3339 in UTC, and its storage class
index.operations/s3/list-fetch-owner: Ask for owners with fetch-owner=true, and report each listed object's owner ID
index.operations/s3/list-first-page: Send page_size as max-keys, and report a truncated page's NextContinuationToken as the continuation token
index.operations/s3/list-key-equal-to-prefix: Report a key that equals the prefix as an entry
index.operations/s3/list-key-equal-to-prefix-d: Report a key that equals the prefix as an entry, and the keys under it as a common prefix
index.operations/s3/list-max-keys-zero: Send page_size 0 as max-keys=0; S3 answers an empty page that is not truncated
index.operations/s3/list-next-page: Send the continuation token as continuation-token, a + in it as %2B, and report an empty token for the last page
index.operations/s3/list-order: Report the entries in the order S3 sends them, without sorting them again
index.operations/s3/list-order-delimited: Report the entries and the common prefixes in the order S3 sends them, each list on its own
index.operations/s3/list-other-delimiter: Send the delimiter the caller names. A general-purpose bucket groups keys at any delimiter, not only /; here a- groups a-1.txt and a-2.txt
index.operations/s3/list-over-1000: List more keys than the service's default page of 1,000 by following the continuation token
index.operations/s3/list-page: List a prefix with ListObjectsV2 (list-type=2), and report each entry's key, size and ETag, quotes included
index.operations/s3/list-prefix-special-charac: Percent-encode the prefix in the query, a space as %20 and a plus as %2B, and decode the common prefixes of a URL-encoded listing as well as the keys
index.operations/s3/list-prefix-without-slash: Match the prefix as the start of the key, not as a directory: object-tests/boa matches object-tests/board/
index.operations/s3/list-separator-keys: Report keys with leading dots, repeated slashes, a space and a trailing slash exactly as stored
index.operations/s3/list-separator-keys-delimi: Group each key at the first delimiter after the prefix, even where the key repeats it or ends with it
index.operations/s3/list-service-unavailable: Report a 503 ServiceUnavailable answer as an error, after at most 5 retries
index.operations/s3/list-start-after: Send start-after, and list only the keys after it
index.operations/s3/list-start-after-delimited: Send a start-after that names no key; it skips the keys and common prefixes up to it
index.operations/s3/list-truncated-without-tok: Report an error when a truncated page carries no continuation token; do not stop early or list from the start again
index.operations/s3/list-unauthenticated: Report the service authorization error for this operation; signature acceptance is tested separately.
index.operations/s3/list-xml-escaped: Read XML character references in listed names, such as & and <, or ask for encoding-type=url and decode the names
index.operations/s3/put-bucket-missing: put bucket missing. A client reports it as container_not_found: the bucket or container is absent, not the object
index.operations/s3/put-computing-crc32: Compute the CRC32 checksum of the body and send it, base64 of its big-endian bytes, in x-amz-checksum-crc32 or in a trailer of an aws-chunked body
index.operations/s3/put-computing-crc32c: Compute the CRC32C checksum of the body and send it, base64 of its big-endian bytes, in x-amz-checksum-crc32c or in a trailer of an aws-chunked body
index.operations/s3/put-computing-crc64nvme: Compute the CRC64NVME checksum of the body and send it, base64 of its big-endian bytes, in x-amz-checksum-crc64nvme or in a trailer of an aws-chunked body
index.operations/s3/put-computing-sha1: Compute the SHA1 checksum of the body and send it, base64 of its big-endian bytes, in x-amz-checksum-sha1 or in a trailer of an aws-chunked body
index.operations/s3/put-computing-sha256: Compute the SHA256 checksum of the body and send it, base64 of its big-endian bytes, in x-amz-checksum-sha256 or in a trailer of an aws-chunked body
index.operations/s3/put-conditional-conflict: Report a 409 ConditionalRequestConflict to a conditional put as an error. AWS advises retrying a put, so a client may retry up to 5 times first, and need not retry
index.operations/s3/put-content-disposition-no: Write a Content-Disposition whose filename is outside ASCII. A general-purpose bucket returns header bytes as it got them, so the UTF-8 bytes read back; an RFC 6266 filename* is stored as written, and any reader decodes it
index.operations/s3/put-content-encoding-gzip: Store Content-Encoding: gzip with a write, and the gzip bytes unchanged
index.operations/s3/put-content-properties: Store Content-Type, Content-Language, Content-Disposition and Cache-Control with a write
index.operations/s3/put-content-type-edge-spac: Write a content type with spaces at either end, which HTTP drops, so the service stores it trimmed. A client may refuse it
index.operations/s3/put-content-type-non-ascii: Write a Content-Type with a parameter outside ASCII as its UTF-8 bytes. A general-purpose bucket returns header bytes as it got them, so they read back
index.operations/s3/put-created-key-space: put created, with the key "space name.txt"
index.operations/s3/put-if-unmodified-since-pa: Report a write with If-Unmodified-Since as an error. S3 takes no date condition on a PutObject and answers 501 NotImplemented. A client may refuse it before sending
index.operations/s3/put-internal-error: Report a 500 InternalError answer as an error, after at most 5 retries
index.operations/s3/put-lost-the-race-to-creat: put lost the race to create
index.operations/s3/put-md5-mismatch: Declared transactional MD5 must cover the exact body bytes; report service rejection of a mismatch.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-names-differ-: S3 matches a metadata name without case. A general-purpose bucket merges two names that differ only in case into one pair, dup: one,two, which does not read back as sent, so refuse the call.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-non-ascii-val: A general-purpose bucket reads header bytes as ISO-8859-1 and decodes an RFC 2047 encoded word. Send é as the byte e9 or as an encoded word, or refuse the value if the client keeps metadata to ASCII; its UTF-8 bytes store cafÃ©.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-outside-latin: No header byte carries 雪, so send it as an RFC 2047 encoded word, or refuse the value if the client keeps metadata to ASCII. A general-purpose bucket stores its UTF-8 bytes as three ISO-8859-1 characters.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-punctuation-n: S3 stores a name that holds any character of an HTTP token, and one that starts with a digit.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-value-control: A control character other than a tab is no valid HTTP field value. Send the value as an RFC 2047 encoded word, which S3 stores and a read decodes again, or refuse it.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-value-edge-wh: HTTP drops spaces and tabs at either end of a header value, so S3 would store a. An RFC 2047 encoded word stores them, but a read returns the value unencoded and loses them again. Send an encoded word, or refuse the value.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-value-encoded: A general-purpose bucket reads each space-separated token that starts with =? and ends with ?= as an RFC 2047 encoded word: it decodes it, or answers 400 or 500 when it cannot. So =?UTF-8?Q?caf=C3=A9?= sent as it is stores café. Wrapped in an encoded word of its own it stores the text, but a read returns it unencoded and decodes it again. Wrap it, or refuse it.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-value-line-br: CR and LF are no valid HTTP field value, and a general-purpose bucket stores each as a space even inside an RFC 2047 encoded word. No request stores the value, so refuse it.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-value-not-an-: A general-purpose bucket reads each space-separated token that starts with =? and ends with ?= as an RFC 2047 encoded word: it decodes it, or answers 400 or 500 when it cannot. Neither a=?b?=c nor x=?UTF-8?Q?caf=C3=A9?=y is such a token, so S3 stores this value as it is sent, and a read returns it. Send it as it is, or wrapped in an encoded word; do not refuse it.
index.operations/s3/put-metadata-value-with-ta: S3 stores a tab inside a value as it is sent. Send it raw, or inside an RFC 2047 encoded word.
index.operations/s3/put-tagging: Replace the tags of an object
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-10-tags: Set 10 tags, the most an object takes
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-11-tags: Report 11 tags, one more than an object takes, as an error. A client may refuse them
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-duplicate-key: Report a tag set that names one key twice as an error. A client may refuse it, or report it unsupported where its API cannot repeat a key
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-invalid-charac: Report a tag key with !, which S3 does not allow, as an error. A client may refuse it
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-key-128: Set a tag whose key has 128 characters, the longest a key may be
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-key-129: Report a tag key of 129 characters, one more than a key may have, as an error. A client may refuse it
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-special-charac: Set a tag with a space and each of + - = . _ : / @, which S3 allows, escaped as XML text
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-value-256: Set a tag whose value has 256 characters, the longest a value may be
index.operations/s3/put-tagging-value-257: Report a tag value of 257 characters, one more than a value may have, as an error. A client may refuse it
index.operations/s3/put-two-checksums: Report S3's refusal of a write with two additional checksums; S3 keeps one checksum per object and answers 400 InvalidRequest to more than one x-amz-checksum- header
index.operations/s3/put-unauthenticated: Report the service authorization error for this operation; signature acceptance is tested separately.
index.operations/s3/put-with-crc32: Send an additional checksum in its x-amz-checksum- header; S3 stores it as the object's one checksum, in place of the CRC64NVME it adds to a write without one
index.operations/s3/put-with-crc32c: Send a CRC32C checksum that the caller gives, in x-amz-checksum-crc32c
index.operations/s3/put-with-crc64nvme: Send a CRC64NVME checksum that the caller gives, in x-amz-checksum-crc64nvme
index.operations/s3/put-with-md5: Carry a declared transactional MD5 without substituting a payload or stored-property hash.
index.operations/s3/put-with-sha1: Send a SHA1 checksum that the caller gives, in x-amz-checksum-sha1
index.operations/s3/put-with-sha256: Send a SHA256 checksum that the caller gives, in x-amz-checksum-sha256
index.operations/s3/put-with-storage-class: Write an object into the STANDARD_IA storage class
index.operations/s3/put-with-tags-duplicate-ke: Report a write whose x-amz-tagging names one key twice as an error. A client may refuse it, or report it unsupported where its API cannot repeat a key
index.operations/s3/put-with-tags-special-char: Write an object with a tag that holds a space and each of + - = . _ : / @, percent-encoded in x-amz-tagging, so that S3 reads + as a plus and not a space
index.operations/s3/put-with-unknown-storage-c: Refuse a storage class that S3 does not have
index.operations/s3/stage-copy: Copy a whole object into a part of a multipart upload, with UploadPartCopy
index.operations/s3/stage-copy-200-internal-er: Report a part copy answered 200 with an InternalError in the body as an error, never as a success. A client may retry up to 5 times first, and need not retry
index.operations/s3/stage-copy-range: Copy bytes 0 to 2 of an object into a part, named in x-amz-copy-source-range with an inclusive end, as bytes=0-2
index.operations/s3/stage-copy-range-beyond-so: Report a part copy whose range ends past the source as an error. S3 answers 400 InvalidArgument
index.operations/s3/stage-copy-source-if-match: Report a part copy whose source does not have the ETag in x-amz-copy-source-if-match as a failed condition, 412 PreconditionFailed, of kind precondition
index.operations/s3/stage-empty-part: Stage an empty part, which S3 takes
index.operations/s3/stage-part-10000: Part numbers run from 1 to 10,000. Stage part 10,000; only 0 and 10,001 may be refused.
index.operations/s3/start-bucket-missing: start bucket missing. A client reports it as container_not_found: the bucket or container is absent, not the object
index.operations/s3/start-content-properties: Start a multipart upload with content properties, which the completed object keeps
index.operations/s3/start-unauthenticated: Report the service authorization error for this operation; signature acceptance is tested separately.
index.operations/s3/start-with-storage-class: Start a multipart upload into a storage class, named in x-amz-storage-class
index.operations/s3/start-with-tags: Start a multipart upload with tags, sent URL-encoded in x-amz-tagging, which the completed object keeps

A directory bucket refuses a header byte outside ASCII, and stores an RFC 2047 encoded word as it came. Send é as an encoded word, or refuse the value if the client keeps metadata to ASCII.
HTTP drops spaces and tabs at either end of a header value, so S3 would store a. Send the value as an RFC 2047 encoded word, which a read decodes again, or refuse it.

A general-purpose bucket reads each space-separated token that starts with =? and ends with ?= as an RFC 2047 encoded word: it decodes it, or answers 400 or 500 when it cannot. A directory bucket stores such a token as it is sent. A client that decodes on a read sends the value wrapped in an encoded word of its own; one that keeps metadata to ASCII sends it as it is.

A general-purpose bucket reads each space-separated token that starts with =? and ends with ?= as an RFC 2047 encoded word: it decodes it, or answers 400 or 500 when it cannot. Neither a=?b?=c nor x=?UTF-8?Q?caf=C3=A9?=y is such a token, so S3 stores this value as it is sent, and a read returns it. Send it as it is, or wrapped in an encoded word; do not refuse it.
A control character other than a tab is no valid HTTP field value. Send the value as an RFC 2047 encoded word, which S3 stores and a read decodes again, or refuse it.
